note: Cue timing is aligned to the dialogue line timecodes in episode_package.json. Dialect tracks are illustrative English glosses that keep the dialect's forms of address (Dadi, beta, beti, bahu, Mama).

source.d02_1: You're slower than the postman, Amar Mama!
source.d02_2: The postman doesn't carry your presents.
source.d02_3: Come inside, beta. This house has been waiting for you.
source.d03_1: In the city they feed you air and call it dinner.
source.d03_2: When the rain remembers the field, the field forgives the drought.
source.d03_3: The will is read tomorrow at ten. Everyone must be present.
source.d04_1: You knew he left it to the trust, didn't you?
source.d04_2: Keep your voice down. The walls have ears.
source.d04_3: You left, Amar. Some of us had to stay.
source.d06_1: Out! City boys can't play on real ground!
source.d06_2: Best of three. The bus ride ruined my wrists.
source.d08_1: Beti, you carry this whole house on your shoulders.
source.d08_3: If they knew what I did with the papers...
source.d09_1: The house and land are placed in the Singh Heritage Trust.
source.d09_2: This is a forgery, and you know it!
source.d09_3: Your grandfather signed it in front of me.
source.d10_1: I hid the will. I had to do it. For the family.
source.d10_2: The trust was going to sell this house and send Dadi away.
source.d11_1: Some of us had to come back.
